title: the DF-4 return-value adapters, one row per member
heading: ## Per-member rows: the getter each return-value adapter calls, and the type it is installed for (OPUS, 2026-10-03)
lead: The DF-4 family (402 members in the frontmatter; {N} get a row here) shares the 26-byte shape of section 2, stated there once and not repeated here: `mov rcx, rdx`, `mov rbx, r8`, one `call`, `mov [rbx], rax`. What differs from member to member is that one `call`: each adapter calls its own getter (no two rows share a target). Each row anchors that call, the member's distinguishing instruction, and states its target and the reflected type T. T is the template argument of every `PClassDescriptor*<T>` vtable that holds the adapter at slot 5 (section 8), read from that vtable's MSVC RTTI type descriptor in the certified image, and every such vtable must agree on T. {CHECK} derives every row from the image and compares it with the committed {ROWS}. A member that is not exactly one direct call fails, and so does a member whose slot-5 vtables disagree on T or whose target or T differs from the row. Two controls are refused: a swapped target and a moved anchor. The getter is given as a bare address, not a citation, because the getters are explained, or not, on their own pages. Only the adapter's anchor counts here, per SWE2-AUDIT-SPEC's ruling `202e59a0a`. Eight DF-4 members get no row, and each is listed with its reason in [`excluded.tsv`](../../_index/candidates/opus-ee-return-value-adapters-1003/excluded.tsv): five are not a single direct call, and three sit in descriptor vtables that do not name one template type T (a non-template descriptor class beside the template one, or several Vectormath types sharing one body). The checker fails if any of them starts deriving. The 46 DF-1 members have no distinguishing instruction (their bodies are identical), so they get no rows.
